edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: Restoring vision improves sensory input, mobility, and social participation; those changes offer a plausible route to slower dementia trajectories.
edges.summary: The anchor for this edge is the 2023 Pham cohort in Clin Ophthalmol, which suggests that cataract surgery tracks with lower risk or better outcomes for dementia (all-cause). Later papers point in much the same direction, so the live uncertainty is usually about effect size or which subgroups carry the signal most strongly.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
